documents.title: Student Generative AI Usage Guidance (UNC AI Committee)
documents.summary: University committee's recommended syllabus language for student use of generative AI. It sets principles (AI should help you think, students own the product, use must be documented) and per-assignment-type guidance, and lets instructors override any of it. Documentation uses a required attestation and usage form.
documents.stance_why: The cover note says 'as the course instructor you can have different guidelines for a specific assignment or exam', and the text is 'recommended language' that instructors adapt; it permits documented AI use 'in principle' and prohibits it on exams unless allowed. Because the instructor decides and the text is a template, it delegates.

units.fit_note: Recommendation to adopt and adapt template language, not a mandate that every syllabus carry an AI statement.

documents.summary: College of Arts & Sciences student guidelines adapted from the university committee text. documents.title: Guidance on Generative AI Use (Graduate School Handbook)
documents.summary: Graduate School handbook guidance that encourages programs to adopt the university committee's philosophy and applies campus student and teaching guidance to graduate students and TAs. For research it recommends discussing AI use with advisors and disclosing it in methods or appendices.
documents.stance_why: The page 'encourages graduate programs to embrace the philosophy' and says 'Individual graduate programs may establish guidelines', and it sets no ban or permission itself; decisions go to programs, advisors and course instructors, so it delegates.

units.why: The Board 'encourages graduate programs to embrace the philosophy' that humans are responsible and 'AI should help you think. Not think for you', so graduate programs are urged to adopt the committee's framework (P56).
units.anchor: encourages graduate programs to embrace the philosophy guiding the recommended language
units.policy: The Graduate School's Administrative Board encourages graduate programs to embrace the philosophy guiding the recommended language that humans are responsible for the use of generative AI and that AI should help you think, not think for you.

units.why: The Board 'maintains that generative AI can be a productive tool and foster new directions and perspectives' (P87).
units.anchor: generative artificial intelligence (AI) can be a productive tool

units.why: 'Users of generative AI... should take full responsibility for their use of AI and any research that might result' (P29).
units.anchor: should take full responsibility for their use of AI and any research
units.frag_start: Users of generative AI, following University guidelines,

units.why: Says generative AI 'may have nuanced applications for graduate students, faculty advisors, and degree program administrators', a recognition that grad context differs (P85).

units.fit_note: Recognizes graduate-specific uses without letting units set rules.

units.why: 'Individual graduate programs may establish guidelines specific to their thesis and comprehensive exams' lets programs set their own rules (P85).
units.anchor: Individual graduate programs may establish guidelines specific to their thesis and comprehensive exams

units.why: 'If generative AI use is encouraged in a program, guidance developed for the campus related to student use should also apply to graduate students' (P56 institution-wide framework applied).

units.policy: If generative AI use is encouraged in a program, guidance developed for the campus related to student use should also apply to graduate students in their own classes and research.
units.fit_note: Applies campus student guidance to graduate students; no framework of its own.

units.why: Programs 'can encourage TAs to connect with supervising faculty to ensure any enrolled student usage complies with class guidelines', which asks TAs to align with the instructor (P109).

units.policy: Programs can encourage TAs to connect with supervising faculty to ensure any enrolled student usage complies with class guidelines.
units.fit_note: Aligns TA handling of student AI use with the supervising faculty's class rules.

units.why: The supervisor must support 'the TA using AI in their own grading/teaching work' - a condition for TA use of AI in grading (P101).

units.policy: Programs can encourage TAs to connect with supervising faculty to ensure the supervisor supports the TA using AI in their own grading/teaching work.
units.fit_note: Covers teaching work generally, not only grading, and makes supervisor support the condition.

units.why: 'Graduate student research is collaborative. Any use of AI for research and writing purposes should be discussed with supervisors, advisors, committee members' (P62 research).

units.policy: Any use of AI for research and writing purposes should be discussed with supervisors, advisors, committee members, and any other associated individuals.
units.fit_note: Calls for discussion with advisors rather than deferring to external venue rules.

units.why: Suggests discussing 'order of writing and editing and using these tools, and how to incorporate its use and permissions for publishing' (P62).
